title: Model vs. User: Whose Values Prevail? Inference-Time Value Alignment in Multi-Turn Conversations
abstract: arXiv:2610.19817v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human values shape how we expect language models to behave. Dominant alignment approaches treat values as global objectives, although the appropriate value orientation is personal and contextual. Training-free alignment can steer models toward target values at inference time, yet has been largely evaluated in single-turn settings and with a single steering direction (e.g., toward safety). We evaluate four prompt- and activation-based steering methods in multi-turn conversations, where user and assistant models push toward the same or opposing, equally desirable values. We track alignment with a linear probe across three models and two value trade-offs. When assistant and user pull in opposite directions, the side matching the assistant's baseline bias often prevails, and effects that look successful early often fade or reverse after a few turns. translated_title: 模型 vs. 用户：谁的价值观占上风？多轮对话中的推理时价值对齐
translated_abstract: 人类价值观塑造了我们对语言模型行为的期望。主流的对齐方法将价值观视为全局目标，然而合适的价值取向实际上是个人的、依赖于具体情境的。无需训练的对齐方法可以在推理时将模型引导至目标价值观，但目前主要在单轮对话设置和单一引导方向（例如朝向安全）下进行评估。我们在多轮对话中评估了四种基于提示和激活的引导方法，其中用户和助手模型朝向相同或相反但同样值得追求的价值观。我们使用线性探针在三个模型和两组价值权衡中追踪对齐情况。当助手和用户朝相反方向拉扯时，与助手基线偏好一致的一方往往占上风，而且早期看似成功的引导效果往往在几轮对话后减弱或反转。因此，引导方法应该在完整对话中、并在价值权衡的两个方向上进行评估。
tldr: 该研究首次在多轮对话中系统评估四种推理时价值引导方法，发现当用户与模型价值观冲突时，与模型基线偏好一致的一方往往胜出，且早期成功的引导效果会在数轮对话后减弱或反转，因此价值对齐应在完整双向对话中评估。
en_tdlr: This study systematically evaluates four inference-time value steering methods in multi-turn conversations, finding that when user and model values conflict, the side matching the model's baseline bias typically prevails, and early successful steering effects often fade or reverse over turns, so value alignment should be evaluated across full bidirectional conversations.
